text: Hello boys and girls, welcome to Sally's class.Nice to see you again.First, let's take a look at what we are going to do in today's class.Look at these two passages.We call them continuous texts.The texts are made up of paragraphs.Here are non-continuous texts.First, let's take a look at the booklet.If you want to know how to feed your three-month-old puppy properly, in which part can you get the useful information?Yes, we can get the information we need in this part.Then, take a look at the contents.If I would like to know something about garden soil problems, which chapter should I read?Right, I should read chapter 2.Please look at the table.Among Tony's neighbors, who threw the most cans last year?Obviously, the whites threw the most cans.We have just got some information from the contents, a booklet, and the table.Do they have anything in common?Some of you may say they have no paragraphs.That's true.Some of you may say they are easy to understand.I agree with you.And some of you may say they can be seen everywhere in our daily life.Actually, the examples we mentioned just now are all non-continuous texts.Let's take a look at other examples.ListsGraphsFlowchartsHave we read any lists, graphs, or flowcharts in the last few years?Actually, we have read quite a lot.Here are some examples.What else have we read?TablesFormsThe examples given above are all non-continuous texts.Well, have you ever thought about the purposes of these non-continuous texts?For example, can you figure out the purpose of the sign?Yes, the writer wants to warn us not to swim or dive here.How about the brochure designed for our summer camp?That's right.The writer wants to persuade us to enter for this summer camp.What about the school library rules?I think the writer wants to tell us what we should do and what we shouldn't do in the school library.That is to say, the writer wants to inform us.Of course, we will meet with other non-continuous texts for other purposes.Now let's get some practice.Please get your worksheet ready.Time is up.Is this text a poster or an advertisement?Yes, it's an advertisement.What does the advertisement tell us?Great, it tells us four of the best beaches in the world.What's the main purpose of the advertisement?I'd like to share my understanding.I think it's to attract more people to these beaches.Do you think so?Well, let's check the answers to the multiple choices.If you want to take photos of White Sand, which beach maybe is not a good choice?Do you think there are any keywords in the sentence?I think white sand and not are the keywords.So we don't need to read the whole passage word for word.We can use scanning.We just need to focus on white sand while reading.Sugar White SandWhite Sand Covered BeachesSugar Fine White SandNow we can get the correct answer.Canapoli BeachThrough this exercise, have you got a good way to select information more efficiently?If Mr.and Mrs.Green from San Francisco visit Canapoli Beach, how much will they at least pay for the round trip airfare?It's your turn to tell me the keywords.Have you got any idea?Canapoli?Anymore?Exactly.We just need to focus on the third famous beach Canapoli to look for the information about airfare.Here, $382 is the price for only one person.Don't forget to multiply it by 2.Which answer should we choose?That's right, we should choose C.Through this exercise, we've learned that sometimes we need to process the information we get.Now let's move on to task 2.It's more challenging.Please read the passage carefully and finish the exercises.In today's class, we've reviewed the features of non-continuous texts.We used scanning to get information.We also practiced processing and combining information.Today's homework.Read the passage on your homework sheet and finish the exercises.That's all for today.Thank you.Goodbye.
